title: Reach the cache without the app-layer glue
description: The usual path from DuckDB to [Redis](https://redis.io/docs/latest/) runs through app-layer Python or Node.js glue. This extension removes it: read and write a live instance from SQL. Best for operational queries, hot-cold data joins, and one-off migrations; for application-grade Redis access, keep a real client.

sections.title: What it is
sections.description: Redis is the most common in-memory cache and quick-lookup store, and it usually sits one network hop away from data you already keep in DuckDB. The normal way to bridge the two is to write a script — pull keys out of Redis in Python or Node, reshape them, load them into a table. This extension removes that middle layer: it exposes Redis operations as `redis_*` SQL functions so the cache becomes just another source you can `SELECT` from, `JOIN` against, and write back to. It is scoped deliberately to the SQL-side workflows where data integration matters — draining a keyspace into a table, joining cached lookups against bulk data, priming a cache from analytical output, auditing keys — rather than to being a complete Redis client.

sections.title: How it works
sections.description: Connection details live in a [DuckDB secret](https://duckdb.org/docs/configuration/secrets_manager) of `TYPE redis`, and every `redis_*` function takes a trailing argument naming that secret. This keeps credentials out of query text and lets dev / staging / prod live as separate secrets you select per query. There is no `ATTACH` interface and no virtual catalog — this is purely a function-based extension, so Redis access composes inline anywhere a scalar function or table function is allowed.

bulletPoints.label: Secret-based configuration
bulletPoints.description: A `redis` secret holds `host`, `port`, and an optional `password` (leave it out when the server has no AUTH). The DuckDB 2.0 build adds `username` (Redis 6 ACL users), `db` (database index) and `timeout_ms`. See [`CREATE SECRET`](https://duckdb.org/docs/sql/statements/create_secret); parameterize the password from the environment so it never lands in a cached query plan.

bulletPoints.label: RESP over TCP
bulletPoints.description: The extension speaks the native [Redis Serialization Protocol](https://redis.io/docs/latest/develop/reference/protocol-spec/) directly over a plain TCP socket — no separate Redis daemon, sidecar, or driver process is involved.

bulletPoints.label: Connection reuse
bulletPoints.description: Connections are pooled and reused across calls rather than reopened per row. In the DuckDB 2.0 build the pool belongs to each database instance and is keyed by host, port, credentials and database index, so a secret never reuses a connection authenticated for another; each thread checks out its own connection, and the commands of a vector of rows are pipelined into one round trip.

bulletPoints.label: Timeouts, cancellation, sandbox
bulletPoints.description: DuckDB 2.0 build: connecting and every wait for reply data are bounded by `redis_timeout_ms` (default 30 s) or the secret's `timeout_ms`, queries waiting on Redis can be interrupted, and every function refuses to run when `enable_external_access` is false.

sections.title: Production caveats
sections.description: Be aware before pointing this at a busy Redis instance. The extension is honest-by-design about what it doesn't yet do.

bulletPoints.label: SCAN, never KEYS
bulletPoints.description: [`KEYS`](https://redis.io/docs/latest/commands/keys/) blocks the Redis server for the duration of the scan — fine in dev, dangerous on production keyspaces. No function here issues it: `redis_keys`, `redis_scan`, and `redis_hscan_over_scan` are all built on cursor-paginated [`SCAN`](https://redis.io/docs/latest/commands/scan/), which iterates without stalling traffic. `redis_keys` and `redis_hscan_over_scan` still walk the whole keyspace, so keep their patterns narrow on large instances.

bulletPoints.label: Strings, hashes, and lists first
bulletPoints.description: Dedicated functions cover strings, hashes, lists, keys and expiry. Sets, sorted sets, streams and other commands go through `redis_command` (DuckDB 2.0 build), which returns text or JSON; there is no PUB-SUB or MULTI/EXEC transaction support. See [Redis data types](https://redis.io/docs/latest/develop/data-types/).

bulletPoints.label: Single-node connections
bulletPoints.description: No [Redis Cluster](https://redis.io/docs/latest/operate/oss_and_stack/management/scaling/) topology awareness. Point the secret at a single endpoint.

bulletPoints.label: Plaintext auth
bulletPoints.description: The `password` field in the secret is sent over plain TCP — TLS is not yet wired up. Use the extension on trusted networks until that lands. See [Redis security](https://redis.io/docs/latest/operate/oss_and_stack/management/security/) for the upstream guidance.

bulletPoints.label: Experimental status
bulletPoints.description: The function surface may change as more Redis primitives land. Pin a known-good extension version in production CTAS jobs.
